United States Mint Opens Sales for the 2023 Morgan and Peace Proof Silver Dollars on August 9
August 4, 2023
WASHINGTON – The United States Mint (Mint) will begin accepting orders for the 2023 Morgan and Peace Proof Silver Dollars on August 9 at noon EDT. Production is limited to 400,000 coins each, and orders are limited to 25 coins per household for the first 24-hour sales period.
The 2023 Morgan and Peace Proof Silver Dollars, both minted at the San Francisco Mint, are priced at $80 each, struck in .999 silver, and have a proof finish. Each coin is encapsulated and packaged in a single, elegant black box with sleeve and accompanied by a Certificate of Authenticity.
Both coins are included in the Mint’s Authorized Bulk Purchase Program.

WASHINGTON – The United States Mint (Mint) today announced that the 2023 Morgan & Peace Dollar Reverse Proof Two-Coin Set (S) will be available at noon (EST) on November 9.
The Morgan & Peace Dollar Reverse Proof Two-Coin Set contains one Morgan Dollar Coin and one Peace Dollar Coin minted at the United States Mint at San Francisco in .999 silver with reverse proof finishes. Each set is encapsulated and packaged in a single, elegant black box with sleeve and accompanied by a Certificate of Authenticity.

United States Mint Opens Sales for the 2023 Morgan and Peace Proof Silver Dollars on August 9
August 4, 2023
WASHINGTON – The United States Mint (Mint) will begin accepting orders for the 2023 Morgan and Peace Proof Silver Dollars on August 9 at noon EDT. Production is limited to 400,000 coins each, and orders are limited to 25 coins per household for the first 24-hour sales period.
The 2023 Morgan and Peace Proof Silver Dollars, both minted at the San Francisco Mint, are priced at $80 each, struck in .999 silver, and have a proof finish. Each coin is encapsulated and packaged in a single, elegant black box with sleeve and accompanied by a Certificate of Authenticity.
Both coins are included in the Mint’s Authorized Bulk Purchase Program. No more than 10% of products with limited quantities are distributed to authorized bulk purchasers under this program.
The 2023 renditions of the Morgan and Peace Silver Dollars feature two of the most revered designs of Liberty in U.S. coinage history. The Morgan Dollar, designed by George T. Morgan, features an obverse profile of Lady Liberty, and the reverse features a heraldic eagle. The Peace Dollar, designed by Anthony de Francisci, features the Goddess of Liberty on the obverse and a bald eagle clutching an olive branch on the reverse.
To sign up for REMIND ME alerts for the Morgan and Peace Proof Silver Dollars (you will need to sign up for an alert for each individual product), visit:
https://catalog.usmint.gov/morgan-2023-silver-dollar-23XF.html
(23XF)
https://catalog.usmint.gov/peace-2023-silver-dollar–23XL.html
(23XL)
Please use the Mint’s catalog site at
https://catalog.usmint.gov/
as your primary source of the most current information on product and service status.
About the United States Mint
Congress created the United States Mint in 1792, and the Mint became part of the Department of the Treasury in 1873. As the Nation’s sole manufacturer of legal tender coinage, the Mint is responsible for producing circulating coinage for the Nation to conduct its trade and commerce. The Mint also produces numismatic products, including proof, uncirculated, and commemorative coins; Congressional Gold Medals; silver and bronze medals; and silver and gold bullion coins.

United States Mint Opens Sales for the 2023 Morgan and Peace Proof Silver Dollars on August 9
August 4, 2023
WASHINGTON – The United States Mint (Mint) will begin accepting orders for the 2023 Morgan and Peace Proof Silver Dollars on August 9 at noon EDT. Production is limited to 400,000 coins each, and orders are limited to 25 coins per household for the first 24-hour sales period.
The 2023 Morgan and Peace Proof Silver Dollars, both minted at the San Francisco Mint, are priced at $80 each, struck in .999 silver, and have a proof finish. Each coin is encapsulated and packaged in a single, elegant black box with sleeve and accompanied by a Certificate of Authenticity.
Both coins are included in the Mint’s Authorized Bulk Purchase Program. No more than 10% of products with limited quantities are distributed to authorized bulk purchasers under this program.
The 2023 renditions of the Morgan and Peace Silver Dollars feature two of the most revered designs of Liberty in U.S. coinage history. The Morgan Dollar, designed by George T. Morgan, features an obverse profile of Lady Liberty, and the reverse features a heraldic eagle. The Peace Dollar, designed by Anthony de Francisci, features the Goddess of Liberty on the obverse and a bald eagle clutching an olive branch on the reverse.
To sign up for REMIND ME alerts for the Morgan and Peace Proof Silver Dollars (you will need to sign up for an alert for each individual product), visit:
https://catalog.usmint.gov/morgan-2023-silver-dollar-23XF.html
(23XF)
https://catalog.usmint.gov/peace-2023-silver-dollar–23XL.html
(23XL)
Please use the Mint’s catalog site at
https://catalog.usmint.gov/
as your primary source of the most current information on product and service status.
About the United States Mint
Congress created the United States Mint in 1792, and the Mint became part of the Department of the Treasury in 1873. As the Nation’s sole manufacturer of legal tender coinage, the Mint is responsible for producing circulating coinage for the Nation to conduct its trade and commerce. The Mint also produces numismatic products, including proof, uncirculated, and commemorative coins; Congressional Gold Medals; silver and bronze medals; and silver and gold bullion coins.

2023 Morgan & Peace Dollar Reverse Proof Two-Coin Set (S) Available November 9 at Noon
November 2, 2023
WASHINGTON – The United States Mint (Mint) today announced that the 2023 Morgan & Peace Dollar Reverse Proof Two-Coin Set (S) will be available at noon (EST) on November 9.
The Morgan & Peace Dollar Reverse Proof Two-Coin Set contains one Morgan Dollar Coin and one Peace Dollar Coin minted at the United States Mint at San Francisco in .999 silver with reverse proof finishes. Priced at $185, the set’s mintage is limited to 250,000, with a household order limit of five in effect for the first 24 hours.
Each set is encapsulated and packaged in a single, elegant black box with sleeve and accompanied by a Certificate of Authenticity.
The set is included in the Mint’s Authorized Bulk Purchase Program. No more than 10% of products with limited quantities will be distributed to authorized bulk purchasers under this program.
The 2023 renditions of the Morgan and Peace Silver Dollars feature two of the most revered designs of Liberty in U.S. coinage history. The Morgan Dollar, designed by George T. Morgan, features an obverse profile of Lady Liberty, and the reverse features a heraldic eagle. The Peace Dollar, designed by Anthony de Francisci, features the Goddess of Liberty on the obverse and a bald eagle clutching an olive branch on the reverse.
To set up REMIND ME alerts for the 2023 Morgan & Peace Dollar Reverse Proof Two-Coin Set (S), please visit:
https://catalog.usmint.gov/morgan-peace-dollar-2023-two-coin-reverse-proof-set-23XS.html/
(product code 23XS).
To view additional United States Mint products, visit
https://catalog.usmint.gov/
.
About the United States Mint
Congress created the United States Mint in 1792, and the Mint became part of the Department of the Treasury in 1873. As the Nation’s sole manufacturer of legal tender coinage, the Mint is responsible for producing circulating coinage for the Nation to conduct its trade and commerce. The Mint also produces numismatic products, including proof, uncirculated, and commemorative coins; Congressional Gold Medals; silver and bronze medals; and silver and gold bullion coins. Its numismatic programs are self-sustaining and operate at no cost to taxpayers.

snippets.snippet: ... Morgan Dollar Coin and one Peace Dollar Coin in .999 silver with reverse proof finishes produced at the Mint facility in San Francisco. The mintage is ...

next_segments.content: [row 2] program: morgan_dollars | slot_id: morgan_dollars_2021_o_privy_2021#O-Privy | catalog_entry_now: O-Privy (app compares mint letter; these coins carry no mint mark, so never match) | proposed_value: P-O-PRIVY (Philadelphia, privy mark) | source_url_1: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Morgan_dollar | source_url_2: https://www.usacoinbook.com/coins/dollars/morgan/ | quote/excerpt: Wikipedia: "Two-thirds of the Philadelphia-minted dollars contained "privy marks" for the now defunct Carson City (CC) and New Orleans (O) mints."; usacoinbook: "2021 P | O Privy Mark | 173,551" | confidence: High | tier_a_url: https://web.archive.org/web/20210709183332/https://www.usmint.gov/coins/coin-medal-programs/morgan-peace-dollar-anniversary-coins/2021-morgan-dollar | tier_a_quote: "The Philadelphia Mint will produce three versions: One without a mint mark to recognize the historic Philadelphia Mint One with an “O” privy mark to recognize the historic Mint in New Orleans, LA One with a “CC” privy mark to recognize the historic Mint in Carson City, NV" | tier_b_url: https://www.pcgs.com/pcgsnolookup/morgan-peace-dollar-reproductions-2021-date/252432 | tier_b_quote: "877710 MS 2021-O Privy $1 Morgan Dollar 100th Anniversary" | source_tier_achieved: A | confidence_revised: High | notes: Tier A = US Mint 2021 Morgan Dollar program page (Wayback 2021-07-09): "The Philadelphia Mint will produce three versions: One without a mint mark ... One with an “O” privy mark ... One with a “CC” privy mark"; the page lists "Mint and Mint Mark Denver Philadelphia San Francisco" (no New Orleans or Carson City). Release of May 2021 (https://web.archive.org/web/20210525060415/https://www.usmint.gov/news/press-releases/united-states-mint-offering-2021-morgan-and-peace-dollars-in-three-pre-order-windows): "The product limit for each Morgan Dollar is 175,000 coins". Limit vs sold: 175,000 vs 21XD "MORGAN SILVER DOLLAR O PRIVY MARK" = 173,551 sold (report valid 9/27/2026). [Cumulative Sales figures from the saved copy of the usmint.gov cumulative-sales data endpoint (saved 2026-10-02); not re-fetchable live on 2026-10-06 (403). These are units sold of each product, not a struck mintage.] So the O is a privy mark on a Philadelphia coin, not a mint mark; P-O-PRIVY is right. Tier B = PCGS Number Lookup "Morgan and Peace Dollar Reproductions (2021 to Date)" (https://www.pcgs.com/pcgsnolookup/morgan-peace-dollar-reproductions-2021-date/252432): "2021-O Privy $1 Morgan Dollar 100th Anniversary" (PCGS writes the privy as "2021-O Privy", a label style; it is not a mint mark). Kept High. PCGS read live with curl on 2026-10-06. usacoinbook and Wikipedia used only as context.

extractive_segments.content: [row 1] program: morgan_dollars | slot_id: morgan_dollars_2023_s_2023#S | catalog_entry_now: S (app reads bare S as NON-proof) | proposed_value: S-SILVER-PROOF (2023-S Morgan is a silver proof; S-PROOF would reject silver) | source_url_1: https://www.usacoinbook.com/coins/dollars/morgan/ | quote/excerpt: usacoinbook: "2023 S | Proof | 383,400" | confidence: High | tier_a_url: https://web.archive.org/web/20230810134920/https://www.usmint.gov/news/press-releases/united-states-mint-opens-sales-for-the-2023-morgan-and-peace-proof-silver-dollars-on-august-9 | tier_a_quote: "Production is limited to 400,000 coins each" … "The 2023 Morgan and Peace Proof Silver Dollars, both minted at the San Francisco Mint, are priced at $80 each, struck in .999 silver, and have a proof finish." | source_tier_achieved: A | confidence_revised: High | notes: Tier B not needed (Tier A achieved). Tier A = US Mint release (Aug 4, 2023) "United States Mint Opens Sales for the 2023 Morgan and Peace Proof Silver Dollars on August 9": both "minted at the San Francisco Mint", ".999 silver", "proof finish". Limit vs sold: limit 400,000 each vs Mint sales 23XF "2023 MORGAN SILVER DOLLAR PROOF (S)" = 366,835 sold (report valid 9/27/2026). [Cumulative Sales figures from the saved copy of the usmint.gov cumulative-sales data endpoint (saved 2026-10-02); not re-fetchable live on 2026-10-06 (403). These are units sold of each product, not a struck mintage.] (usacoinbook's 383,400 is not the Mint sales figure; note only.) The coin is a silver proof, so the bare S id (read by the app as non-proof) should become S-SILVER-PROOF. Kept High. United States Mint Opens Sales for the 2023 Morgan and Peace Proof Silver Dollars on August 9
August 4, 2023
WASHINGTON – The United States Mint (Mint) will begin accepting orders for the 2023 Morgan and Peace Proof Silver Dollars on August 9 at noon EDT. Production is limited to 400,000 coins each, and orders are limited to 25 coins per household for the first 24-hour sales period.
The 2023 Morgan and Peace Proof Silver Dollars, both minted at the San Francisco Mint, are priced at $80 each, struck in .999 silver, and have a proof finish. Each coin is encapsulated and packaged in a single, elegant black box with sleeve and accompanied by a Certificate of Authenticity.
Both coins are included in the Mint’s Authorized Bulk Purchase Program. No more than 10% of products with limited quantities are distributed to authorized bulk purchasers under this program.
The 2023 renditions of the Morgan and Peace Silver Dollars feature two of the most revered designs of Liberty in U.S. coinage history. The Morgan Dollar, designed by George T. Morgan, features an obverse profile of Lady Liberty, and the reverse features a heraldic eagle. The Peace Dollar, designed by Anthony de Francisci, features the Goddess of Liberty on the obverse and a bald eagle clutching an olive branch on the reverse.
To sign up for REMIND ME alerts for the Morgan and Peace Proof Silver Dollars (you will need to sign up for an alert for each individual product), visit:
https://catalog.usmint.gov/morgan-2023-silver-dollar-23XF.html
(23XF)
https://catalog.usmint.gov/peace-2023-silver-dollar–23XL.html
(23XL)
Please use the Mint’s catalog site at
https://catalog.usmint.gov/
as your primary source of the most current information on product and service status.
About the United States Mint
Congress created the United States Mint in 1792, and the Mint became part of the Department of the Treasury in 1873. As the Nation’s sole manufacturer of legal tender coinage, the Mint is responsible for producing circulating coinage for the Nation to conduct its trade and commerce. The Mint also produces numismatic products, including proof, uncirculated, and commemorative coins; Congressional Gold Medals; silver and bronze medals; and silver and gold bullion coins.

next_segments.content:
Its numismatic programs are self-sustaining and operate at no cost to taxpayers.
Note: To ensure that all members of the public have fair and equal access to United States Mint products, the United States Mint will not accept and will not honor orders placed prior to the official on-sale date of August 9, 2023.

2023 Morgan & Peace Dollar Reverse Proof Two-Coin Set (S) Available November 9 at Noon
November 2, 2023
WASHINGTON – The United States Mint (Mint) today announced that the 2023 Morgan & Peace Dollar Reverse Proof Two-Coin Set (S) will be available at noon (EST) on November 9.
The Morgan & Peace Dollar Reverse Proof Two-Coin Set contains one Morgan Dollar Coin and one Peace Dollar Coin minted at the United States Mint at San Francisco in .999 silver with reverse proof finishes. Priced at $185, the set’s mintage is limited to 250,000, with a household order limit of five in effect for the first 24 hours.
Each set is encapsulated and packaged in a single, elegant black box with sleeve and accompanied by a Certificate of Authenticity.
The set is included in the Mint’s Authorized Bulk Purchase Program. No more than 10% of products with limited quantities will be distributed to authorized bulk purchasers under this program.
The 2023 renditions of the Morgan and Peace Silver Dollars feature two of the most revered designs of Liberty in U.S. coinage history. The Morgan Dollar, designed by George T. Morgan, features an obverse profile of Lady Liberty, and the reverse features a heraldic eagle. The Peace Dollar, designed by Anthony de Francisci, features the Goddess of Liberty on the obverse and a bald eagle clutching an olive branch on the reverse.
To set up REMIND ME alerts for the 2023 Morgan & Peace Dollar Reverse Proof Two-Coin Set (S), please visit:
https://catalog.usmint.gov/morgan-peace-dollar-2023-two-coin-reverse-proof-set-23XS.html/
(product code 23XS).
To view additional United States Mint products, visit
https://catalog.usmint.gov/
.
About the United States Mint
Congress created the United States Mint in 1792, and the Mint became part of the Department of the Treasury in 1873. As the Nation’s sole manufacturer of legal tender coinage, the Mint is responsible for producing circulating coinage for the Nation to conduct its trade and commerce. The Mint also produces numismatic products, including proof, uncirculated, and commemorative coins; Congressional Gold Medals; silver and bronze medals; and silver and gold bullion coins. Its numismatic programs are self-sustaining and operate at no cost to taxpayers.

2023 Morgan & Peace Dollar Reverse Proof Two-Coin Set (S) Available November 9 at Noon
November 2, 2023
WASHINGTON – The United States Mint (Mint) today announced that the 2023 Morgan & Peace Dollar Reverse Proof Two-Coin Set (S) will be available at noon (EST) on November 9.
The Morgan & Peace Dollar Reverse Proof Two-Coin Set contains one Morgan Dollar Coin and one Peace Dollar Coin minted at the United States Mint at San Francisco in .999 silver with reverse proof finishes. Priced at $185, the set’s mintage is limited to 250,000, with a household order limit of five in effect for the first 24 hours.
Each set is encapsulated and packaged in a single, elegant black box with sleeve and accompanied by a Certificate of Authenticity.
The set is included in the Mint’s Authorized Bulk Purchase Program. No more than 10% of products with limited quantities will be distributed to authorized bulk purchasers under this program.
The 2023 renditions of the Morgan and Peace Silver Dollars feature two of the most revered designs of Liberty in U.S. coinage history. The Morgan Dollar, designed by George T. Morgan, features an obverse profile of Lady Liberty, and the reverse features a heraldic eagle. The Peace Dollar, designed by Anthony de Francisci, features the Goddess of Liberty on the obverse and a bald eagle clutching an olive branch on the reverse.
To set up REMIND ME alerts for the 2023 Morgan & Peace Dollar Reverse Proof Two-Coin Set (S), please visit:
https://catalog.usmint.gov/morgan-peace-dollar-2023-two-coin-reverse-proof-set-23XS.html/
(product code 23XS).
To view additional United States Mint products, visit
https://catalog.usmint.gov/
.
About the United States Mint
Congress created the United States Mint in 1792, and the Mint became part of the Department of the Treasury in 1873. As the Nation’s sole manufacturer of legal tender coinage, the Mint is responsible for producing circulating coinage for the Nation to conduct its trade and commerce. The Mint also produces numismatic products, including proof, uncirculated, and commemorative coins; Congressional Gold Medals; silver and bronze medals; and silver and gold bullion coins. Its numismatic programs are self-sustaining and operate at no cost to taxpayers.

Description
Morgan Dollar Enhanced Uncirculated Coin
250TH Anniversary with “1776 ~ 2026” dual date and a Liberty Bell Privy Mark
Designed by George T. Morgan
Each stunning silver Enhanced Uncirculated coin is struck in .999 fine silver
Packaged in an elegant blue presentation box
Includes certificate of authenticity
Minted at the United States Mint in West Point
The United States 250th Anniversary Morgan Dollar commemorates the Semiquincentennial of American independence with a masterful reinterpretation of this beloved coin design. The Morgan Dollar was designed by Mint Chief Engraver George T. Morgan (1845 – 1925) and minted from 1878 to 1904 and again in 1921. This iconic silver dollar represented the country’s westward expansion and industrial development in the late 19th century. Blending historic artistry with contemporary symbolism, this Morgan Dollar is more than a coin—it is a tangible reflection of America’s past, present, and enduring promise for the future.
This special one-year issue of the Morgan Dollar bears the dates “1776 ~ 2026” and a unique Liberty Bell privy mark with the numeral “250.” The obverse features Liberty in profile. A cap, flora, and a crown incused with the word “LIBERTY” adorn her head, while 13 stars, “E PLURIBUS UNUM,” “1776 ~ 2026” encircle her and anchor the design in a sweeping narrative of 250 years of independence.
The reverse depicts an eagle with outstretched wings clasping arrows and an olive branch, accompanied by a wreath. Reverse inscriptions are “UNITED STATES OF AMERICA,” “IN GOD WE TRUST,” and “ONE DOLLAR.”
The coin is encapsulated and placed in a stylish clamshell within an elegant blue presentation box. The box is adorned with the official United States Mint seal; the outer sleeve incorporates an image of the obverse coin design. This high-quality coin is accompanied by a certificate of authenticity bearing an image of the obverse. This commemorative enhanced uncirculated finish Morgan Dollar – forged in lustrous 99.9% silver— stands as a lasting tribute to the enduring ideals of the United States and sure to be a collector favorite for years to come.

Description
Morgan Dollar Enhanced Uncirculated Coin
250TH Anniversary with “1776 ~ 2026” dual date and a Liberty Bell Privy Mark
Designed by George T. Morgan
Each stunning silver Enhanced Uncirculated coin is struck in .999 fine silver
Packaged in an elegant blue presentation box
Includes certificate of authenticity
Minted at the United States Mint in West Point
The United States 250th Anniversary Morgan Dollar commemorates the Semiquincentennial of American independence with a masterful reinterpretation of this beloved coin design. The Morgan Dollar was designed by Mint Chief Engraver George T. Morgan (1845 – 1925) and minted from 1878 to 1904 and again in 1921. This iconic silver dollar represented the country’s westward expansion and industrial development in the late 19th century. Blending historic artistry with contemporary symbolism, this Morgan Dollar is more than a coin—it is a tangible reflection of America’s past, present, and enduring promise for the future.
This special one-year issue of the Morgan Dollar bears the dates “1776 ~ 2026” and a unique Liberty Bell privy mark with the numeral “250.” The obverse features Liberty in profile. A cap, flora, and a crown incused with the word “LIBERTY” adorn her head, while 13 stars, “E PLURIBUS UNUM,” “1776 ~ 2026” encircle her and anchor the design in a sweeping narrative of 250 years of independence.
The reverse depicts an eagle with outstretched wings clasping arrows and an olive branch, accompanied by a wreath. Reverse inscriptions are “UNITED STATES OF AMERICA,” “IN GOD WE TRUST,” and “ONE DOLLAR.”
The coin is encapsulated and placed in a stylish clamshell within an elegant blue presentation box. The box is adorned with the official United States Mint seal; the outer sleeve incorporates an image of the obverse coin design. This high-quality coin is accompanied by a certificate of authenticity bearing an image of the obverse. This commemorative enhanced uncirculated finish Morgan Dollar – forged in lustrous 99.9% silver— stands as a lasting tribute to the enduring ideals of the United States and sure to be a collector favorite for years to come.

About the United States Mint
Congress created the United States Mint in 1792, and the Mint became part of the Department of the Treasury in 1873. As the Nation’s sole manufacturer of legal tender coinage, the Mint is responsible for producing circulating coinage for the Nation to conduct its trade and commerce. The Mint also produces numismatic products, including proof, uncirculated, and commemorative coins; Congressional Gold Medals; silver and bronze medals; and silver and gold bullion coins. Its numismatic programs are self-sustaining and operate at no cost to taxpayers.
Note: To ensure that all members of the public have fair and equal access to United States Mint products, the United States Mint will not accept and will not honor orders placed prior to the official on-sale date of November 21, 2024, at noon EST.

United States Mint 2024 Morgan and Peace Dollar Reverse Proof Two-Coin Set™  Now Available
United States Mint 2024 Morgan and Peace Dollar Reverse Proof Two-Coin Set™  Now Available
November 26, 2024
WASHINGTON – The United States Mint (Mint) 2024 Morgan and Peace Dollar Reverse Proof Two-Coin Set is now available for purchase. Released on November 21, the set is priced at $215 and contains one Morgan Dollar Coin and one Peace Dollar Coin in .999 silver with reverse proof finishes produced at the Mint facility in San Francisco. The mintage is limited to 262,500, with a household order limit of five in effect for the first 24 hours.
Each set is encapsulated and packaged in a single, elegant blue box with a sleeve, and accompanied by a certificate of authenticity.
The 2024 renditions of the Morgan and Peace Silver Dollars feature two of the most revered designs of Liberty in U.S. coinage history. The Morgan Dollar, designed by George T. Morgan, features an obverse profile of Lady Liberty, and the reverse features a heraldic eagle. The Peace Dollar, designed by Anthony de Francisci, features the Goddess of Liberty on the obverse and a bald eagle clutching an olive branch on the reverse.
Orders are being accepted at:
https://www.usmint.gov/morgan-and-peace-dollar-2024-two-coin-reverse-proof-set-24XS.html
.
The Morgan and Peace Dollar Reverse Proof Two-Coin Set is also available at the Mint’s sales centers at the Philadelphia Mint, 151 N. Independence Mall East, Philadelphia, PA 19106 (on 5th Street between Arch Street and Race Street); at the Denver Mint, 320 West Colfax Avenue, Denver, CO 80204 (on Cherokee Street, between West Colfax Avenue and West 14th Avenue); and from the United States Mint Headquarters Coin Store in Washington, D.C., 801 9th St., NW; Washington, DC 20220.
The set is included in the Mint’s Authorized Bulk Purchase Program. No more than 10% of products with limited quantities will be distributed to authorized bulk purchasers under this program.
Please use the United States Mint website at
https://www.usmint.gov/shop/
as your primary source of the most current information on product and service status or call 1-800-USA-MINT (872-6468). Hearing and speech impaired customers with TTY equipment may order by calling 1-888-321-MINT (6468).

United States Mint Opens Sales for the 2024 Morgan and Peace Uncirculated Silver Dollars on July 11
July 3, 2024
WASHINGTON – The United States Mint (Mint) is pleased to announce that the 2024 Morgan and Peace Uncirculated Silver Dollars will go on sale on July 11 at noon EDT. Production is limited to 275,000 coins each, and orders are limited to 25 coins per household for the first 24-hour sales period.
The 2024 Morgan and Peace Uncirculated Silver Dollars—both minted at the Philadelphia Mint—are priced at $91 each, struck in .999 silver, and have an uncirculated finish.
Designed by former Mint Chief Engraver George T. Morgan, the Morgan Dollar obverse (heads) features Liberty in profile. A cap, flora, and a crown incused with the word “LIBERTY” adorn her head, while 13 stars, “E PLURIBUS UNUM,” and “2024” encircle her.
The Morgan Dollar reverse (tails) depicts an eagle with outstretched wings clasping arrows and an olive branch, accompanied by a wreath. Reverse inscriptions are “UNITED STATES OF AMERICA,” “IN GOD WE TRUST,” and “ONE DOLLAR.”
The Peace Dollar was designed by renowned Italian American Sculptor Anthony de Francisci. The obverse features Liberty in profile, a radiant crown on her head. The inscriptions are “LIBERTY,” “IN GOD WE TRUST,” and “2024.”
The Peace Dollar reverse depicts an eagle at rest holding an olive branch above the inscription “PEACE.” Additional inscriptions are “UNITED STATES OF AMERICA,” “E PLURIBUS UNUM,” and “ONE DOLLAR.”
Each coin is encapsulated and comes in a blue clamshell presentation case that is placed in an outer box and sleeve and is accompanied by a Certificate of Authenticity.
Both coins are included in the Mint’s Authorized Bulk Purchase Program. Products listed in this program will be eligible for early release, carry an AB suffix in the product code, and carry a premium. Early released products are not eligible for discounts. No more than 10% of products with limited quantities will be distributed to authorized bulk purchasers.

United States Mint Opens Sales for the 2024 Morgan and Peace Uncirculated Silver Dollars on July 11
July 3, 2024
WASHINGTON – The United States Mint (Mint) is pleased to announce that the 2024 Morgan and Peace Uncirculated Silver Dollars will go on sale on July 11 at noon EDT. Production is limited to 275,000 coins each, and orders are limited to 25 coins per household for the first 24-hour sales period.
The 2024 Morgan and Peace Uncirculated Silver Dollars—both minted at the Philadelphia Mint—are priced at $91 each, struck in .999 silver, and have an uncirculated finish.
Designed by former Mint Chief Engraver George T. Morgan, the Morgan Dollar obverse (heads) features Liberty in profile. A cap, flora, and a crown incused with the word “LIBERTY” adorn her head, while 13 stars, “E PLURIBUS UNUM,” and “2024” encircle her.
The Morgan Dollar reverse (tails) depicts an eagle with outstretched wings clasping arrows and an olive branch, accompanied by a wreath. Reverse inscriptions are “UNITED STATES OF AMERICA,” “IN GOD WE TRUST,” and “ONE DOLLAR.”
The Peace Dollar was designed by renowned Italian American Sculptor Anthony de Francisci. The obverse features Liberty in profile, a radiant crown on her head. The inscriptions are “LIBERTY,” “IN GOD WE TRUST,” and “2024.”
The Peace Dollar reverse depicts an eagle at rest holding an olive branch above the inscription “PEACE.” Additional inscriptions are “UNITED STATES OF AMERICA,” “E PLURIBUS UNUM,” and “ONE DOLLAR.”
Each coin is encapsulated and comes in a blue clamshell presentation case that is placed in an outer box and sleeve and is accompanied by a Certificate of Authenticity.
Both coins are included in the Mint’s Authorized Bulk Purchase Program. Products listed in this program will be eligible for early release, carry an AB suffix in the product code, and carry a premium. Early released products are not eligible for discounts. No more than 10% of products with limited quantities will be distributed to authorized bulk purchasers.

United States Mint Opens Sales for the 2023 Morgan and Peace Proof Silver Dollars on August 9
August 4, 2023
WASHINGTON – The United States Mint (Mint) will begin accepting orders for the 2023 Morgan and Peace Proof Silver Dollars on August 9 at noon EDT. Production is limited to 400,000 coins each, and orders are limited to 25 coins per household for the first 24-hour sales period.
The 2023 Morgan and Peace Proof Silver Dollars, both minted at the San Francisco Mint, are priced at $80 each, struck in .999 silver, and have a proof finish. Each coin is encapsulated and packaged in a single, elegant black box with sleeve and accompanied by a Certificate of Authenticity.
Both coins are included in the Mint’s Authorized Bulk Purchase Program. No more than 10% of products with limited quantities are distributed to authorized bulk purchasers under this program.
The 2023 renditions of the Morgan and Peace Silver Dollars feature two of the most revered designs of Liberty in U.S. coinage history. The Morgan Dollar, designed by George T. Morgan, features an obverse profile of Lady Liberty, and the reverse features a heraldic eagle. The Peace Dollar, designed by Anthony de Francisci, features the Goddess of Liberty on the obverse and a bald eagle clutching an olive branch on the reverse.
To sign up for REMIND ME alerts for the Morgan and Peace Proof Silver Dollars (you will need to sign up for an alert for each individual product), visit:
https://catalog.usmint.gov/morgan-2023-silver-dollar-23XF.html
(23XF)
https://catalog.usmint.gov/peace-2023-silver-dollar–23XL.html
(23XL)
Please use the Mint’s catalog site at
https://catalog.usmint.gov/
as your primary source of the most current information on product and service status.
About the United States Mint
Congress created the United States Mint in 1792, and the Mint became part of the Department of the Treasury in 1873. As the Nation’s sole manufacturer of legal tender coinage, the Mint is responsible for producing circulating coinage for the Nation to conduct its trade and commerce. The Mint also produces numismatic products, including proof, uncirculated, and commemorative coins; Congressional Gold Medals; silver and bronze medals; and silver and gold bullion coins.

2023 Morgan & Peace Dollar Reverse Proof Two-Coin Set (S) Available November 9 at Noon
November 2, 2023
WASHINGTON – The United States Mint (Mint) today announced that the 2023 Morgan & Peace Dollar Reverse Proof Two-Coin Set (S) will be available at noon (EST) on November 9.
The Morgan & Peace Dollar Reverse Proof Two-Coin Set contains one Morgan Dollar Coin and one Peace Dollar Coin minted at the United States Mint at San Francisco in .999 silver with reverse proof finishes. Priced at $185, the set’s mintage is limited to 250,000, with a household order limit of five in effect for the first 24 hours.
Each set is encapsulated and packaged in a single, elegant black box with sleeve and accompanied by a Certificate of Authenticity.
The set is included in the Mint’s Authorized Bulk Purchase Program. No more than 10% of products with limited quantities will be distributed to authorized bulk purchasers under this program.
The 2023 renditions of the Morgan and Peace Silver Dollars feature two of the most revered designs of Liberty in U.S. coinage history. The Morgan Dollar, designed by George T. Morgan, features an obverse profile of Lady Liberty, and the reverse features a heraldic eagle. The Peace Dollar, designed by Anthony de Francisci, features the Goddess of Liberty on the obverse and a bald eagle clutching an olive branch on the reverse.
To set up REMIND ME alerts for the 2023 Morgan & Peace Dollar Reverse Proof Two-Coin Set (S), please visit:
https://catalog.usmint.gov/morgan-peace-dollar-2023-two-coin-reverse-proof-set-23XS.html/
(product code 23XS).
To view additional United States Mint products, visit
https://catalog.usmint.gov/
.
About the United States Mint
Congress created the United States Mint in 1792, and the Mint became part of the Department of the Treasury in 1873. As the Nation’s sole manufacturer of legal tender coinage, the Mint is responsible for producing circulating coinage for the Nation to conduct its trade and commerce. The Mint also produces numismatic products, including proof, uncirculated, and commemorative coins; Congressional Gold Medals; silver and bronze medals; and silver and gold bullion coins. Its numismatic programs are self-sustaining and operate at no cost to taxpayers.

Note: To ensure that all members of the public have fair and equal access to United States Mint products, the United States Mint will not accept and will not honor orders placed prior to the official on-sale date of November 9, 2023, at noon EST.

As the Nation’s sole manufacturer of legal tender coinage, the Mint is responsible for producing circulating coinage for the Nation to conduct its trade and commerce. The Mint also produces numismatic products, including proof, uncirculated, and commemorative coins; Congressional Gold Medals; silver and bronze medals; and silver and gold bullion coins. Its numismatic programs are self-sustaining and operate at no cost to taxpayers.

United States Mint 2024 Morgan and Peace Dollar Reverse Proof Two-Coin Set™  Now Available
United States Mint 2024 Morgan and Peace Dollar Reverse Proof Two-Coin Set™  Now Available
November 26, 2024
WASHINGTON – The United States Mint (Mint) 2024 Morgan and Peace Dollar Reverse Proof Two-Coin Set is now available for purchase. Released on November 21, the set is priced at $215 and contains one Morgan Dollar Coin and one Peace Dollar Coin in .999 silver with reverse proof finishes produced at the Mint facility in San Francisco. The mintage is limited to 262,500, with a household order limit of five in effect for the first 24 hours.
Each set is encapsulated and packaged in a single, elegant blue box with a sleeve, and accompanied by a certificate of authenticity.
The 2024 renditions of the Morgan and Peace Silver Dollars feature two of the most revered designs of Liberty in U.S. coinage history. The Morgan Dollar, designed by George T. Morgan, features an obverse profile of Lady Liberty, and the reverse features a heraldic eagle. The Peace Dollar, designed by Anthony de Francisci, features the Goddess of Liberty on the obverse and a bald eagle clutching an olive branch on the reverse.
Orders are being accepted at:
https://www.usmint.gov/morgan-and-peace-dollar-2024-two-coin-reverse-proof-set-24XS.html
.
The Morgan and Peace Dollar Reverse Proof Two-Coin Set is also available at the Mint’s sales centers at the Philadelphia Mint, 151 N. Independence Mall East, Philadelphia, PA 19106 (on 5th Street between Arch Street and Race Street); at the Denver Mint, 320 West Colfax Avenue, Denver, CO 80204 (on Cherokee Street, between West Colfax Avenue and West 14th Avenue); and from the United States Mint Headquarters Coin Store in Washington, D.C., 801 9th St., NW; Washington, DC 20220.
The set is included in the Mint’s Authorized Bulk Purchase Program. No more than 10% of products with limited quantities will be distributed to authorized bulk purchasers under this program.
Please use the United States Mint website at
https://www.usmint.gov/shop/
as your primary source of the most current information on product and service status or call 1-800-USA-MINT (872-6468). Hearing and speech impaired customers with TTY equipment may order by calling 1-888-321-MINT (6468).

About the United States Mint
Congress created the United States Mint in 1792, and the Mint became part of the Department of the Treasury in 1873. As the Nation’s sole manufacturer of legal tender coinage, the Mint is responsible for producing circulating coinage for the Nation to conduct its trade and commerce. The Mint also produces numismatic products, including proof, uncirculated, and commemorative coins; Congressional Gold Medals; silver and bronze medals; and silver and gold bullion coins. Its numismatic programs are self-sustaining and operate at no cost to taxpayers.
Note: To ensure that all members of the public have fair and equal access to United States Mint products, the United States Mint will not accept and will not honor orders placed prior to the official on-sale date of November 21, 2024, at noon EST.

United States Mint 2024 Morgan and Peace Dollar Reverse Proof Two-Coin Set™  Now Available
United States Mint 2024 Morgan and Peace Dollar Reverse Proof Two-Coin Set™  Now Available
November 26, 2024
WASHINGTON – The United States Mint (Mint) 2024 Morgan and Peace Dollar Reverse Proof Two-Coin Set is now available for purchase. Released on November 21, the set is priced at $215 and contains one Morgan Dollar Coin and one Peace Dollar Coin in .999 silver with reverse proof finishes produced at the Mint facility in San Francisco. The mintage is limited to 262,500, with a household order limit of five in effect for the first 24 hours.
Each set is encapsulated and packaged in a single, elegant blue box with a sleeve, and accompanied by a certificate of authenticity.
The 2024 renditions of the Morgan and Peace Silver Dollars feature two of the most revered designs of Liberty in U.S. coinage history. The Morgan Dollar, designed by George T. Morgan, features an obverse profile of Lady Liberty, and the reverse features a heraldic eagle. The Peace Dollar, designed by Anthony de Francisci, features the Goddess of Liberty on the obverse and a bald eagle clutching an olive branch on the reverse.
Orders are being accepted at:
https://www.usmint.gov/morgan-and-peace-dollar-2024-two-coin-reverse-proof-set-24XS.html
.
The Morgan and Peace Dollar Reverse Proof Two-Coin Set is also available at the Mint’s sales centers at the Philadelphia Mint, 151 N. Independence Mall East, Philadelphia, PA 19106 (on 5th Street between Arch Street and Race Street); at the Denver Mint, 320 West Colfax Avenue, Denver, CO 80204 (on Cherokee Street, between West Colfax Avenue and West 14th Avenue); and from the United States Mint Headquarters Coin Store in Washington, D.C., 801 9th St., NW; Washington, DC 20220.
The set is included in the Mint’s Authorized Bulk Purchase Program. No more than 10% of products with limited quantities will be distributed to authorized bulk purchasers under this program.
Please use the United States Mint website at
https://www.usmint.gov/shop/
as your primary source of the most current information on product and service status or call 1-800-USA-MINT (872-6468). Hearing and speech impaired customers with TTY equipment may order by calling 1-888-321-MINT (6468).

About the United States Mint
Congress created the United States Mint in 1792, and the Mint became part of the Department of the Treasury in 1873. As the Nation’s sole manufacturer of legal tender coinage, the Mint is responsible for producing circulating coinage for the Nation to conduct its trade and commerce. The Mint also produces numismatic products, including proof, uncirculated, and commemorative coins; Congressional Gold Medals; silver and bronze medals; and silver and gold bullion coins. Its numismatic programs are self-sustaining and operate at no cost to taxpayers.
Note: To ensure that all members of the public have fair and equal access to United States Mint products, the United States Mint will not accept and will not honor orders placed prior to the official on-sale date of November 21, 2024, at noon EST.

2025 Morgan and Peace Dollar Proof Coins Available on September 11
2025 Morgan and Peace Dollar Proof Coins Available on September 11
September 4, 2025
WASHINGTON, Sept. 4, 2025 — The United States Mint (Mint) will begin accepting orders for the
2025 Morgan Dollar Proof Coin (product code 25XF)
and
2025 Peace Dollar Proof Coin (product code 25XL)
on Thursday, September 11 at noon EDT. Production is limited to 180,000 units for the Morgan Dollar and 170,000 for the Peace Dollar.  For each product, orders are limited to 10 coins per household for the first 24 hours of sales.
Both the Morgan and Peace Dollar Proof Coins will be sold via the Mint’s website, the toll-free number, 1-800-USA-MINT (872-6468), and at the Mint’s sales centers at the
Philadelphia Mint
, the
Denver Mint
, and the
Mint Headquarters Coin Store
in Washington, D.C.
The 2025 Morgan and Peace Dollars are struck at the San Francisco Mint, rendered in 99.9% fine silver with a reeded edge, and priced at $95 each.
Each coin is encapsulated and packaged in a single, elegant blue box with a sleeve and with an accompanying Certificate of Authenticity.

2025 Morgan and Peace Dollar Proof Coins Available on September 11
2025 Morgan and Peace Dollar Proof Coins Available on September 11
September 4, 2025
WASHINGTON, Sept. 4, 2025 — The United States Mint (Mint) will begin accepting orders for the
2025 Morgan Dollar Proof Coin (product code 25XF)
and
2025 Peace Dollar Proof Coin (product code 25XL)
on Thursday, September 11 at noon EDT. Production is limited to 180,000 units for the Morgan Dollar and 170,000 for the Peace Dollar.  For each product, orders are limited to 10 coins per household for the first 24 hours of sales.
Both the Morgan and Peace Dollar Proof Coins will be sold via the Mint’s website, the toll-free number, 1-800-USA-MINT (872-6468), and at the Mint’s sales centers at the
Philadelphia Mint
, the
Denver Mint
, and the
Mint Headquarters Coin Store
in Washington, D.C.
The 2025 Morgan and Peace Dollars are struck at the San Francisco Mint, rendered in 99.9% fine silver with a reeded edge, and priced at $95 each.
Each coin is encapsulated and packaged in a single, elegant blue box with a sleeve and with an accompanying Certificate of Authenticity.

next_segments.content:
As the Nation’s sole manufacturer of legal tender coinage, the Mint is responsible for producing circulating coinage for the Nation to conduct its trade and commerce. The Mint also produces numismatic products, including proof, uncirculated, and commemorative coins; Congressional Gold Medals; silver and bronze medals; and silver and gold bullion coins. Its numismatic programs are self-sustaining and operate at no cost to taxpayers.
